members.note: In the style: how many dots a project's spinners have is a theme decision, and the control rebuilds its piece pool on every push.

Slate's rule, kept: the piece is SCALED on the ticked axis by the same wave that drives its opacity, so it swells as it brightens. One wave for both rather than a second clock. Off by default, which is what this throbber has always drawn.

A float where UMG has a bool, and it says more: MinOpacity 1 is UMG's bAnimateOpacity off (every piece stays solid), and anything less is how faint a piece gets at the bottom of its cycle. GetAnimateOpacity / SetAnimateOpacity spell UMG's bool over it.
FDreamUIFaceBrush rather than FSlateBrush -- a piece is a procedural rect and the brush is its body texture. Empty is the plain rounded dot.
Rebuilds the piece pool, which is what a count IS here. Edits this instance's style; see UDreamBorder::SetPadding for the caveat about a project sheet.
Turning it off re-places every piece, so a piece frozen mid-pulse does not keep the width the last tick gave it.
Off pins the floor at 1; on restores the shipped floor only when the floor is currently 1, so switching off and on is not a way to lose a hand-tuned value.
UThrobber has no style struct; this is the family's spelling, and the one call that rebuilds the piece pool.
